S.C. gas prices up again 

by City Paper Staff September 28, 2026September 28, 2026

Share this:

  • Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook
  • Share on X (Opens in new window) X
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:03
Instaread

MORNING HEADLINES  |  South Carolina gas prices rose another 4.5 cents last week to $4.08 a gallon, or about $1.30 more than this time last year, according to price tracker GasBuddy. Nationally, there was a slight decline.

The lowest Palmetto State price recorded last week was $3.59. The highest was $5.99. 

“With oil holding below $100 per barrel, many Americans may see modest declines ahead for gasoline and slight drops for diesel,” GasBuddy analyst Patrick De Haan said in a Sept. 28 release. 

But, he added, “The broader geopolitical situation remains fluid and could push prices in either direction with little warning, and with Trump still weighing a diesel export ban, impacts could follow.”

In related news, President Trump this weekend rejected an Iranian ceasefire plan that promised to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key Mideast oil shipment route whose closure has contributed to high U.S. gas prices.

CP NEWS: Thirst for the 1st: Honeycutt, Lacore want to serve in Congress. It’s hard for Democrats not to hear the hopeful echoes of 2018 in this year’s 1st Congressional District race between Republican Charleston County Council member Jenny Costa Honeycutt and retired Admiral Nancy Lacore.

LOCAL: S.C. Ports’ slump continued over summer. Newly released figures show container volume was down 8% in July and August, with operating revenue falling 20% to just over $60 million.
